pages.api:
# API reference

> The stream, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Stream `audio.pcm/<name>`

`pcm.s16le.v1`, class `stream`: 640-byte records (20 ms of 16 kHz mono s16le) while speaking, none when idle. `t_ns` is the wall clock when the chunk was written.

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `spoken`, `dropped`, `failures`, `audio` (s), `synth.time` (s), `stream.seq`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout

`{"speaking": "...", "audio_ms": N}` per text, then one report per interval:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `voice` | string | the engine, `synthetic`, `none` |
| `spoken`, `dropped`, `failures` | numbers | since start |
| `audio_s`, `real_time_factor` | numbers | speech produced; synthesis time over speech time |
| `queued`, `speaking` | number, bool | |
| `last_text`, `last_error` | string/null | |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `stream_open`, `seq`, `error` |

## Store vector (id 36)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | `spoken` |
| 1 | `rtf` |
| 2 | `audio_s` |
| 3 | `dropped` |
| 4 | `failures` |
| 5 | `queued` |
| 6 | `bus_connected` |
| 7 | `stream_seq` |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8070`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--source`, `--name`, `--engine`, `--speaker`, `--speed`, `--threads`, `--python`, `--models-root`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-tts --once --simulate                          # a tone per word
cog-tts --once --replay lines.jsonl --engine piper # lines {"text": "..."}, the real voice
cog-tts                                            # continuous; speaks transcript/reply0
```

With a broker (`WEFTOS_COGBUS`, `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN`) the speech goes to `audio.pcm/tts0`; without one the cog synthesizes and reports but has nowhere to write. Each spoken text is printed as `{"speaking": ..., "audio_ms": ...}`.

## Placed on a node

Place `tts` in the same project as `assistant` and `audio-out`. Its `cog.toml` declares the input `transcript` and the outputs `audio.pcm` (a stream) and `telemetry`. It declares no device; `audio-out` owns the speaker.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Give the board a voice that any cog can use, through one stream.

`tts` reads text from `transcript/<source>` (default `reply0`, the `assistant`'s answers), turns it into speech and writes it, in real time, to the stream `audio.pcm/<name>` (default `tts0`). The `audio-out` cog plays that stream.

## The short path

1. **Check the models.** Kokoro and Piper files and a Python with sherpa-onnx must exist. → see **The voice**
2. **Try it without a model.** `cog-tts --once --simulate` speaks a tone per word and reports the length.
3. **Speak a file of lines.** `cog-tts --once --replay lines.jsonl` with `{"text": "..."}` per line.
4. **Place it with `audio-out`.** Start `audio-out` with `--source tts0`. → see **Set up**

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- Synthesis runs on the CPU. Measured on the Ventuno at three threads: Piper makes speech in about a tenth of its length (a 5 s answer in half a second), Kokoro in about 1.1 times its length (a 4 s sentence in 4.7 s). Piper is the default for that reason; Kokoro is more natural but too slow for a conversation unless given more threads.
- Speech is written at real time, one 20 ms chunk each, so a long answer occupies the stream for its whole length; new text waits behind it (at most four waiting, then the oldest is dropped).
- There is no interrupting speech that has started.
- The voices are English.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `the synthesizer worker did not become ready` | the model or Python is missing, or loading took over two minutes | check **The voice**; run the worker by hand |
| `<path>: No such file or directory` | the Python path is wrong | set **Python** |
| `no broker: WEFTOS_COGBUS is not set` | run from a shell without a broker | use `--simulate` or `--replay`, or place the cog |

## Text arrives but nothing is heard

- `spoken` grows but `bus.stream_open` is false: no stream. Check `bus.error`.
- The stream is written but `audio-out` plays nothing: check that `audio-out` reads the same name (`--source tts0`).
- Check the speaker's volume and mute (`amixer`).

## `dropped` grows

Text arrives faster than it can be spoken. The assistant's answers are capped at 400 characters; lower **Answer length** there.

## `failures` grows

`last_error` holds the worker's message. The worker keeps serving after an error.
pages.voice:
# The voice

> Which engine speaks, and where its files live.

The cog starts one worker process and talks to it in JSON lines. The worker is a short Python script carried inside the cog (`worker/tts_worker.py`); it loads the engine through **sherpa-onnx** and returns mono float32 samples, which the cog resamples to 16 kHz and cuts into 640-byte chunks.

| Engine | Files under the models directory | Native rate |
|---|---|---|
| `kokoro` | `kokoro-en-v0_19/` (`model.onnx`, `voices.bin`, `tokens.txt`, `espeak-ng-data`) | 24 000 Hz |
| `piper` | `vits-piper-en_US-amy-medium/` (`en_US-amy-medium.onnx`, `tokens.txt`, `espeak-ng-data`) | 22 050 Hz |

Defaults: Python `/data/bench/venv-tts/bin/python` (or `$TTS_PYTHON`), models in `/data/bench/models`. **Speaker** picks a Kokoro voice by number; **Speed** is 0.5 to 2.0 times normal.

Start-up loads the model and speaks a warm-up sentence into nowhere; the report says `no_source` until then.

## What is spoken

The text with control characters turned to spaces, whitespace collapsed and a limit of 600 characters.

# Sensor guide for tts (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "Speech synthesis on a Linux board"
sensor = "Text from the assistant, spoken through audio-out"
cog = "tts"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "voice", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
voice = "voice"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "transcript/reply0"
detail = "text to speak"

[[flow]]
name = "Synthesizer worker"
detail = "Kokoro or Piper, CPU"

[[flow]]
name = "Resampler"
detail = "to 16 kHz mono s16le"

[[flow]]
name = "audio.pcm/tts0"
detail = "20 ms chunks, real time"
